December 17, 1940.

Government schools in the French Concession -
contemplated taking over by the Nanking Authorities.

With reference to the attached press article
on the above subject which appeared on the December 6 and
7 issue of the Shanghai Evening Post and the China Press
respectively, enquiries have been made and the following
ascertained.

The following schools which, prior to the
outbreak of the hostilities on August 13, 1937, were
administered by the Chinese Chungking authorities, have
been slated for taking over by the Nanking (Wang Ching
Wei) Government :-

1. National Chiaotung University (国立交通大学),
   45 Avenue Victor Emmanuel III.

2. Middle School Department of the National Chinan
   University (国立暨大附中), Passage 41,
   Route Dollfus.

3. Kiangsu Provincial Middle School of Shanghai
   (江苏省立上海中学), 440 Rue du Marche.

4. Hsiao Kwong Middle School (晓光中学),
   694 Avenue Joffre.

5. Hwa Tung Middle School for Girls (华东女中),
   462 Avenue Joffre.

6. Min Li Middle School for Girls (民立女中),
   612 Rue Lafayette.

7. Hwei Kiu Middle School for Girls (怀久女中),
   77 Route Pichon.

（印：16 DEC. 1940 COMMISSAIRE）

关于上述主题，参见附载的分别刊登于12月6日和7日《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）和《字林西报》（China Press）的新闻报道，经查询，查明情况如下。

以下学校在1937年8月13日战事爆发前由重庆的中国当局管理，现已被南京（汪精卫）政府列为接管对象：

Persistent effort by way of inducement have been made by the Nanking authorities for some time past to the principals of these schools for their surrender. The latter however, have remained loyal to the National Government (Chungking).

At the end of November, 1940, Mr. Sung Iah Ting (宋怡亭), secretary of the Educational Department of the French Municipal Council was approached by the Nanking authorities with a request for him to negotiate with the principals of those schools. Mr. Sung subsequently proposed to the principals concerned that instead of the Nanking authorities actually taking over the administration of these schools, new principals should be appointed by the French Municipal Council and that should the present incumbents choose to remain at their posts, nominal appointments would be given them as a matter of form. His proposal however was again turned down by the principals of these schools and all efforts of the Nanking authorities have since proved a total failure.

In view of the situation in the French Concession, which can hardly be considered as favourable to educational institutions affiliated with the Chungking Government, the schools concerned have removed their important documents and files elsewhere as a precaution and in anticipation of a forcible taking over. It is reliably learned that the seven schools would rather close down than submit to the control of the Nanking Regime.

It is further learned that in the event of taking over, the schools will continue to hold classes

南京当局在过去一段时间里，一直通过利诱手段，持续向这些学校的校长施压，要求其交出学校控制权。然而，后者仍忠于国民政府（重庆）。

1940年11月底，南京当局接触了法公董局教育处秘书宋怡亭先生（Mr. Sung Iah Ting），请求他与这些学校的校长进行谈判。随后，宋先生向相关校长提议，不由南京当局实际接管这些学校的管理权，而是由法公董局任命新校长；如果现任校长选择留任，将给予他们名义上的任命以作形式。然而，这一提议再次被这些学校的校长拒绝，自此南京当局的所有努力均彻底失败。

鉴于法租界的局势很难被认为有利于隶属于重庆政府的教育机构，相关学校已将重要文件和档案转移至他处以作预防，并 anticipated（预期）可能发生的强行接管。据可靠消息，这七所学校宁愿关闭，也不愿服从南京政权的控制。

另获悉，一旦发生接管，各校将继续上课

pages.en:
Schools May Suspend As Wang
Men Said Taking Over Control

Voluntary suspension of many
schools for Chinese in French-
town loomed large yesterday
when reports were circulated
that French municipal authori-
ties had agreed to the taking
over of the control of the
schools by representatives of
the Wang Ching-wei regime.
Informed quarters interviewed by
THE CHINA PRESS indicated that the
reports were true and that the mea-
sure would affect not only the
primary and secondary schools in
the Concession but also several
colleges, including the National
Chiaotung University.

Confirmation of the reports
was not available at official
quarters although a high
official of a well-known school
in the Concession stated that
his school had been visited
several times by agents of the
Nanking regime and its records
and documents examined.

20,000 Affected

In all, about 20,000 students would
be affected by the measure alleged-
ly adopted by the Concession.
Educational quarters stated last
night that several of the leading
schools would simply suspend
operation at the closing of the
current semester or at such time
when Nanking agents start taking
over the control of the institutions.

The same quarters added that
repeated efforts had been made by
Mr. Wang's agents here to obtain
the registration of the schools, both
in the Settlement and Concession,
with the Nanking regime. While a
few of the institutions were known
to have obtained such registrations,
the majority of them considered the
change unnecessary.

Co-operation Sought

To what extent Mr. Wang's
regime will assume control of the
Frenchtown schools beyond the re-
quirement that the schools register
with Nanking could not be ascer-
tained yesterday. Speculation was
rife that in the case of the leading
schools, including the Hwa Tung
Girls' Middle School on Avenue
Joffre, Hwei Chu School for Girls
on Route Pichon and the Wei
Chung Middle School on Route de
Zikawei, new principals would be
appointed by the Nanking educa-
tional authorities.

Efforts were also said to have
been made for several months by
Mr. Wang's agents here to solicit
the co-operation of many school
teachers. Several teachers have
told THE CHINA PRESS that they
had been offered large sums of
money if they agree to continue
their teaching at their school when
Nanking takes over their ad-
ministration.

（批：D.I. Paris.
Engrs please.
Puby
12）
pages.zh:
汪派人称将接管控制权
学校或将停课

昨日有传闻称，法市政当局已同意由汪精卫政权代表接管学校控制权，法租界内许多华人学校自愿停课的可能性大幅上升。《字林西报》采访的消息灵通人士指出，这些报道属实，该措施不仅会影响租界内的小学和中学，还将波及包括国立交通大学在内的几所学院。

虽然官方部门无法证实这些报道，但租界内一所知名学校的高级官员表示，南京政权的特工曾多次造访该校，并查阅了其记录和文件。

两万人受影响

据悉，法租界采取的这项措施将影响约20,000名学生。教育界人士昨晚表示，几所主要学校将在本学期结束时，或在南京特工开始接管机构控制权时，直接停止运作。

同一消息来源补充说，汪先生的代理人在此已多次努力，要求公共租界和法租界的学校向南京政权注册。虽然已知少数机构已获得此类注册，但大多数学校认为此举没有必要。

寻求合作

除了要求学校向南京注册外，汪政权将在多大程度上接管法租界学校的控制权，昨日尚无法确定。猜测盛行，认为对于主要学校，包括霞飞路的华东女子中学、毕勋路的惠中女校（Hwei Chu School for Girls，注：此处原文为Hwei Chu，与前文Hwei Kiu不同，依原文译）以及徐家汇路（Route de Zikawei）的位育中学（Wei Chung Middle School，音译），南京教育当局将任命新校长。

据说，汪先生的代理人在此也已数月努力，争取许多学校教师的合作。几位教师告诉《字林西报》，如果他们同意在南京接管学校行政后继续在校任教，他们将获得巨额金钱。

（批：巴黎情报局。
请工程师处理。
Puby
12）

Nanking To Get
Middle Schools
In Concession

French Said Agreeing
To Place 200.000
Tots Under Wang

Six leading middle schools, in-
cluding the Hwa Tung Middle
School and the Wei Chu Middle
School for Girls, in the French
Concession will be handed over to
officials appointed by the Nanking
Regime shortly before the end of
this semester, authoritative circles
told the Evening Post today.

This is understood to be the
first step toward the control of
some 450 primary schools both in
the International Settlement and
the French Concession. If this
measure is effected, around 200,000
Chinese boys and girls will be un-
der the influence of educators ap-
pointed by Nanking.

Chungking Connections

The six middle schools were
understood to have close connec-
tions with Chungking officials, as
their former school masters are
prominent figures in free China at
present.

Leading primary schools in the
French Concession were said to be
preparing to close down after the
end of the present school semester
on January 18, 1941.

This measure, however, by no
means marks the prelude of a pos-
sible mass resignation of all the
teachers in the schools. One pro-
minent primary school master in
the French Concession, when in-
terviewed by the Evening Post this
morning, stated that he would
simply close down his school when
this semester ends and would not
consider re-opening next year.
pages.zh:
南京将接管
租界内的中学

据称法国同意将20万
儿童置于汪氏管辖之下

今日权威人士告诉《晚邮报》，包括华东中学和维初女子中学（Wei Chu Middle School for Girls，音译）在内的法租界六所主要中学，将在本学期结束前不久移交给南京政权任命的官员。

据了解，这是控制国际租界和法租界内约450所小学的第一步。如果实施此项措施，约20万名中国男女学生将受到南京任命的教育工作者的影响。

与重庆的关系

据了解，这六所中学与重庆官员有着密切联系，因为它们的前任校长目前都是自由中国的知名人物。

据说，法租界的主要小学正准备在1941年1月18日本学期结束后关闭。

然而，这一措施绝不标志着所有学校教师可能大规模辞职的前奏。法租界一位著名的小学校长今早接受《晚邮报》采访时表示，他将在本学期结束时直接关闭学校，并且不考虑明年重新开学。

江苏省立中学——活动情况
------------------------------------

关于附载的1941年1月19日《申报》（Sing Pao）一篇关于江苏省立中学会议文章的译文，南通中学校长夏毅昌先生（Mr. HSIAO IH CHANG），地址为静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）105号591弄（中港总，Zung Kong Tsung，音译），于1月21日接受问询，获得如下信息：

1937年中日战事爆发后，约十五所由江苏省政府（重庆政府）建立和/或资助的中学从内地迁至上海。这些学校包括：

南通中学                静安寺路105号591弄。
苏州女子师范学校               新闸路（Sinza Road）1826号。
松江中学             静安寺路141号591弄。
松江女子中学             福煦路（Avenue Foch）1246号。
苏州中学               福州路53号。
镇江中学             江西路（Jinkee Road）97号。
镇江师范学校             宁波路1号363弄。
常州中学             爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII）960号。
无锡中学                爱文义路（Love Lane）。
扬州中学              高乃伊路（Rue Corneille）。
扬州中学第二部              南京路慈渡大楼（Tsze Dzo Building，音译）。
上海中学              马尔斯路（Rue de Marche）440号。

These schools are reported to have been subsidized in the
neighbourhood of $100,000.00 each by Kiangsu Provincial
Government for each half year, but this amount has been
either reduced considerably or has practically been
discontinued because of the Sino-Japanese hostilities and
as a result, the teaching staff are greatly affected.
On January 14, at about 4 p.m., an informal
meeting was held in the Nantung Middle School, Lane 591,
105 Bubbling Well Road, at which the following persons were
present :
WOO TSENG CHIA (吴增芥) - Dean of the Soochow
Normal School for Girls, 1626 Sinza Road.

Middle School, Lane 591, 141 Bubbling
Well Road.

Middle School, Lane 591, 105 B'well Road.
TSANG ZUNG YIEN(章慎言) - - do -

WONG TSENG LING(黄振麟) - - do -
LIU CHING CHI (刘景琦) - - do -
TSAI TSE FENG . (蔡次凤) - - do -

a discussion took place in connection with the improvement
pages.zh:

据报道，这些学校每半年获得江苏省政府约100,000.00美元的补贴，但由于中日战事，这笔金额已大幅减少或实际上已停止发放，因此教职员受到极大影响。
1月14日下午4时许，在静安寺路105号591弄的南通中学举行了一次非正式会议，出席人员如下：
吴增芥（WOO TSENG CHIA）——苏州女子师范学校教务长，新闸路1626号。
朱争衡（CHU PING HENG）——太仓师范学校教师。
李剑青（LI CHIEN TSING）——松江中学教师，静安寺路141号591弄。
徐天游（HSU TIEN YUE）——南通中学教师，静安寺路105号591弄。
章慎言（TSANG ZUNG YIEN）——同上
张舜俞（TSANG SUNG YUE）——同上
黄振麟（WONG TSENG LING）——同上
刘景琦（LIU CHING CHI）——同上

吴增芥主持会议，会议期间讨论了改善

pages.en:
- 3 -

of treatment. It was suggested that the Ministry of
Education of the National Government (Chungking Government)
be requested to render relief to the teaching staff in the
employ of the middle schools established by the Kiangsu
Provincial Government, and that a further meeting be held
in the Nantung Middle School on January 17, 1941.
    In the afternoon of January 17, some twenty
teachers of the middle schools concerned attended, and
before the meeting took place, a Chinese named CHU ( 朱 )
appeared at the Nantung Middle School, Lane 591, 105 Bubbling
Well Road. He claimed to have been despatched
by the "Western Authorities" for the purpose of making
enquiries into the meeting which was to be held in the
school premises, but did not give any definite information
as to which organ he represented. The visitor interviewed
Mr. HSIA SHIH CHANG, Principal of the Nantung Middle School
and warned him against holding the proposed meeting on the
premises and before departure, the self-styled appointee
of the "Western Authorities" stated that any attempt on the
part of Mr. HSIA or other teachers to hold meetings would
result in unpleasant consequences. Mr. HSIA explained
that the meeting was free of any political matter and that
he was not concerned with any political party but agreed to
cancel the meeting. Since this visit, Mr. HSIA has not
attended the school.
pages.zh:

待遇的问题。有人建议请求国民政府（重庆政府）教育部对受雇于江苏省立中学的教职员提供救济，并定于1941年1月17日在南通中学举行进一步会议。
    1月17日下午，约二十名相关中学的教师出席了会议。在会议开始前，一名姓朱（CHU）的中国人出现在静安寺路105号591弄的南通中学。他声称受“西方当局”派遣，目的是调查即将在校舍内举行的会议，但未提供其代表哪个机构的确切信息。这位访客会见了南通中学校长夏世昌先生（Mr. HSIA SHIH CHANG，注：此处英文名与上文夏毅昌不同，依原文译），警告他不要在校舍内举行拟议的会议，并在离开前，这位自称“西方当局”任命的人表示，夏先生或其他教师任何试图举行会议的行为都将导致不愉快的后果。夏先生解释说，会议不涉及任何政治事务，他也不参与任何政党，但同意取消会议。自此次访问以来，夏先生未再到校。

pages.en:
- 4 -

The principal went on to state that he was
informed by a school servant that during the evening of
January 20, at about 6 p.m., three male Chinese called at
the Nantung Middle School, Lane 381, 105 Bubbling Well Road,
and enquiries for the principal but left shortly afterwards
when they found he was not there.

These schools are not in receipt of grant-in-aids
from the Council.

Certified true copy
JHS.
pages.zh:

校长接着表示，他从一名校役处得知，1月20日晚6时许，三名中国男子来到位于静安寺路105号381弄（注：此处门牌弄号与前文591弄不一致，依原文译）的南通中学，询问校长下落，但在发现他不在后不久便离开了。

这些学校未从公董局获得补助金。

核证无误副本
JHS.

Bubbling Well Road. He claimed to have been despatched
by the "Western Authorities" for the purpose of making
enquiries into the meeting which was to be held in the
school premises, but did not give any definite information
as to which organ he represented. The visitor interviewed
Mr. HSIA SHIH CHANG, Principal of the Nantung Middle School
and warned him against holding the proposed meeting on the
premises and before departure, the self-styled appointee
of the "Western Authorities" stated that any attempt on the
part of Mr. HSIA or other teachers to hold meetings would
result in unpleasant consequences. Mr. HSIA explained
that the meeting was free of any political matter and that
he was not concerned with any political party but agreed to
cancel the meeting. Since this visit, Mr. HSIA has not
attended the school.

REPORT
Date February 4, 1941.
Subject Nantung Middle School - Situation.
Made by I.S.I. Forwarded by O. L. Stanford.

On the morning of February 4, Mr. HSIA SHIH CHANG
(夏世昌), principal of the Nantung Middle School, Lane
305, Bubbling Well Road, called at
Special Branch Headquarters and reported concerning the
dismissed students. Mr. HSIA stated that recently some
thirty students were discharged as their school course was
below the standard required and their behaviour was unsatis-
factory. The school authorities are prepared to recommend
these students for study in other local schools, but a number
of the dismissed students are opposed to this procedure and
demand that they be allowed to continue their studies in the
Nantung Middle School. The principal went on to state
that he had received information that a few of the discharged
students have the intention of resorting to some illegal
activity in order to enforce their demands. Among those
dismissed is one TSOONG KWAI SUNG (鍾槐森), residing at
444 Chekiang Road, near Ningpo Road, who is said to be the
most active in the agitation. Mr. HSIA states that TSOONG
KWAI SUNG has been recommended for study in the Hwa Hwa
Middle School, Lane 384, 4 Foochow Road, and had been
promised a certificate when he attains the standard required
but he is said to be dissatisfied with this arrangement.

In view of possible agitation on the part of
the dismissed students against the Nantung Middle School,
Mr. HSIA requests that the Police adopt precautionary measures
at the institute, which will re-open on February 5, 1941.

2月4日上午，南通中学校长夏世昌先生（住址：静安寺路305弄，原文可能有误，前文为105号涌泉邨591弄）来到特别支部总部，就学生被开除一事进行报告。夏先生称，最近约有三十名学生因学业低于规定标准且行为不佳而被开除。校方准备推荐这些学生到本地其他学校就读，但部分被开除的学生反对这一程序，并要求允许他们继续在南通中学就读。校长接着陈述，他收到消息，少数被开除的学生意图采取非法活动以强制实现其要求。在被开除者中，有一人名叫钟槐森（Tsoong Kwai Sung），住在浙江路444号，近宁波路，据称是煽动活动最活跃分子。夏先生称，已推荐钟槐森到福州路4号384弄的华华中学就读，并承诺在他达到规定标准时颁发证书，但据说他对这一安排不满意。

鉴于被开除学生可能对南通中学进行煽动，夏先生请求警方在该机构于1941年2月5日重新开学时采取预防措施。

Trouble with and alleged intimidation
by students of the Nantung Middle school.
House No. 105, Lane 591 Bubbling Well Rd.
--------------------------------------------------

At 9.15.p.m. on 22.10.1940 one named Tsu Yih Ping
( / ), teacher of the Nantung Middle School, 105/591 Bubbling
Well Road, came to station with a letter from the Principal of the
school stating that following trouble with some of the students
a number of loafers had visited the school on the afternoon of the
22.10.1940, had intimidated the faculty and students, had taken
charge of the school office, had cut the telephone wires and,
after causing considerable damage within the office had left taking
with them certain books and papers, property of the school.

Enquiries were made by D.S.I.Guess and C.D.C.226
but little information could be obtained from informant and a visit
was, therefore, paid to the school where the principal, Au Sz Tsong
( 区世宗 ) was interviewed. From him it was ascertained that
about two weeks ago one of the male students, Zau Yau Ding ( 赵耀庭 )
was found together with a female student, Tsu Tse Sung ( 周志生 )
in an empty room of the school. Their conduct aroused suspicion
and they were later interviewed and warned against further improper
conduct. The warning had no effect and, after several further
warnings the two students were taken before the principal and
their fathers were later communicated with by letter and requested
to withdraw both students from the school. This order came into
effect on 10.10.1940 and the two students subsequently removed their
property from the school and discontinued their studies.

南通中学学生制造的麻烦及涉嫌恐吓。
静安寺路105号，591弄。
--------------------------------------------------

1940年10月22日晚上9:15，一名名为祖一平（Zu Yih Ping，音译）的男子，系静安寺路105/591号南通中学教师，持该校校长来信来到警署，信中指出，在与部分学生发生纠纷后，一群闲散人员于1940年10月22日下午到访学校，恐吓教职员工和学生，接管了学校办公室，切断电话线，并在办公室内造成相当程度的破坏后离开，带走了学校的某些书籍和文件等财产。

特别巡官盖斯（Guess）和华籍侦探226号进行了查询，但从报案人处获得的资料甚少，因此前往学校访问，会见了校长区世宗（Au Sz Tsong）。从中获悉，约两周前，一名男学生赵耀庭（Zau Yau Ding）被发现与一名女学生周志生（Tsu Tse Sung）在学校的一间空房间内在一起。他们的行为引起怀疑，随后对他们进行了问询，并警告他们不得再有不当行为。警告无效，经过数次进一步警告后，这两名学生被带到校长面前，随后通过信函联系他们的父亲，要求将两名学生退学。该命令于1940年10月10日生效，随后两名学生从学校搬走其物品并停止学业。

25 10 40

pages.en:
At about 2.00.p.m. on 22.10.1940 the two expelled
students, accompanied by a large crowd of male Chinese who also
appeared to be of student type but were unknown to the masters of
the school, arrived at the school and proceeded to the office on
the first floor where they took possession ordering the principal
to vacate same as they proposed to hold a meeting (conference).
Others of the party informed the students to cease their examinat-
ions as a general meeting of the students was to be held. The
front and rear doors of the school were then closed and guarded
by the visitors. The two expelled students later addressed the
then idle students stating that they were expelled for talking
and that the masters and supervisor of the school were useless.
They called upon the students to discontinue their studies immed-
iately and remain idle until the principal, supervisor and certain
masters had been removed.

At about 4.30.p.m. the visitors declared the meeting
closed and stated that they would return at 10.a.m. on 23.10.40.
In leaving, those persons who had occupied the principal's office
took with them certain books etc. as follows:-

(1) Documents belong to the Principal.
(2) Record of previous school meetings.
(3) Record of previous school announcements.
(4) Several private letters.
(5) School registers.
(6) Keys of offices etc.

In his letter of complaint the principal referred to the
damage caused to the private office but when questioned regarding
this it appeared that no material damage was done and that this
portion of the letter referred to the removal of documents etc.
pages.zh:
1940年10月22日下午约2时，两名被开除的学生在一群看似也是学生模样、但校方并不认识的华籍男子簇拥下抵达学校，径直前往二楼办公室并占据该处，命令校长腾出办公室，声称他们打算在此召开会议。随行人员告知在校学生停止考试，称将举行全体学生大会。随后，学校的前后门均被关闭，并由这些外来人员把守。这两名被开除的学生随后向当时无所事事的学生发表讲话，声称他们因交谈而被开除，并称学校的教员和监学无能。他们号召学生立即停课，保持闲置状态，直至校长、监学及某些教员被撤换为止。

下午约4时30分，来访者宣布会议结束，并表示将于1940年10月23日上午10时返回。离开时，那些占据校长办公室的人带走了以下书籍等物品：

(1) 属于校长的文件。
(2) 以往校务会议记录。
(3) 以往学校公告记录。
(4) 几封私人信件。
(5) 学校注册簿。
(6) 办公室等的钥匙。

校长在投诉信中提到其私人办公室遭受损坏，但在就此接受询问时，似乎并未造成实质性损坏，信中的这一部分指的是文件等物品被拿走一事。

pages.en:
As regards the telephone it is ascertained that same is
situated on the 3rd.floor of the same building but in an adjoining
house also used as a school. There is an arrangements whereby
both schools have use of the telephone. During the affair on the
22.10.1940 the telephone wire was cut, apparently by the visitors.
This cannot definitely be stated but it is known that the cutting
was done during the period referred to above. This damage has
already been made good.

When interviewed on the night of 22.10.1940 Mr. Au Sz Tsong
stated that he did not wish to take any action against the persons
concerned in the affair but, owing to veiled insinuations that they
were sponsored and that some were armed, he feared further trouble
and wished four C.P.Cs to be posted at the school to maintain
the safety of the students. This matter was referred to Insp.Lees
on 23.10.1940 and the necessary arrangements made.

On the morning of the 23.10.1940 C.D.S.66 was detailed to
attend the school and at 10.a.m. the expelled student Zau Yau Ding
presented himself and again addressed the students also presenting
12 demands to the Principal. This man was later questioned by
Insp.Fang and C.D.S.66 and admitted having taking the books etc.
from the office and of concealing them in the students' quarters.
These were returned to the principal. In leaving Zau Yau Ding
was warned against further intimidation of the faculty or inter-
ference with the school working and agreed not to commit any
such acts in the future.

This matter is now considered closed but this report is
submitted for reference.

（左侧批注：Sen.Det.I/s. D.D.O."A" Divn.）
（右侧签名：JOLees D.S.I.）
pages.zh:
关于电话，经查实，电话位于同一栋建筑的三楼，但在隔壁也用作校舍的房屋内。双方学校有一项安排，可共同使用这部电话。在1940年10月22日的事件期间，电话线被切断，显然是由来访者所为。虽然无法确切断定，但已知切断行为发生在上述时间段内。此损坏已修复。

1940年10月22日晚接受问询时，Au Sz Tsong先生（音译）表示，他不希望对事件相关人员采取任何行动，但由于有人暗示这些人有后台支持且部分人持有武器，他担心发生进一步的麻烦，希望派遣四名中国巡捕（C.P.Cs.）驻守学校以维护学生安全。此事于1940年10月23日转交Lees督察处理，并作出了必要安排。

1940年10月23日上午，刑事侦缉股第66号探员（C.D.S.66）被派往学校。上午10时，被开除的学生Zau Yau Ding（音译）现身，再次向学生发表讲话，并向校长提出了12项要求。此人随后受到Fang督察和刑事侦缉股第66号探员的讯问，承认从办公室拿走了书籍等物品，并将其藏匿在学生宿舍。这些物品已归还给校长。离开时，Zau Yau Ding受到警告，不得再恐吓教职员或干扰学校运作，他同意今后不再从事此类行为。

此事现被视为已结案，但提交本报告以备查考。

（左侧批注：高级侦探督察/分部 “A” 区副主管。）
（右侧签名：J.O. Lees 副高级督察。）

pages.en:
Sir,

I beg to lay my humble complaint before you.

On the afternoon of 24-10-46 a party of people about
thirty in number, rushed into the school premises.
They forced the coolies to hand over them the keys and
entered the principal's office, wherein they removed some
important documents, records of conferences and some
personal letters. The members of the party kept guards at
various gates and cut the telephone wire,
detaining all the teachers and students to lose their liberty.

In view of the above I am sending you this letter with
the hope that you will look into the case and have
the men arrested and punished.

A list of stolen property is attached herewith:-

(1) Documents belonging to the Principal.
(2) Record of previous school meetings.
(3) Record of various school announcements.
(4) Several private letters
(5) School registers.
(6) Moveables etc.

I remain,

Yours truly,

Hsia S. Chong,
Principal of the Nantung
Middle School.
pages.zh:
阁下：

谨向您呈递鄙人的申诉。

1946年10月24日下午，一群约三十人闯入校园。
他们强迫苦力交出钥匙，
进入校长办公室，从中取走了一些
重要文件、会议记录和一些
私人信件。这群人在
各个门口把守，并切断了电话线，
拘禁所有师生，剥夺其自由。

鉴于上述情况，特致函阁下，
希望您调查此案，
逮捕并惩处这些人。

随函附上失窃物品清单：

(1) 属于校长的文件。
(2) 以往校务会议记录。
(3) 各类学校公告记录。
(4) 几封私人信件
(5) 学校注册簿。
(6) 动产等。

此致

敬礼

夏士昌（Hsia S. Chong），
南通中学校长。

pages.en:
DEMANDS

1. To dismiss Tsang Tung Yue.
2. To proclaim the regulations of school and dormitory.
3. that a "Joint Class Association" be established, in order
to foster co-operation between teachers and students.
4. That the teachers are not allowed to interfere with any
meeting held, or to offer any suggestion.
5. That dismissal or reprimand of students cannot be put
in force indiscrimately.
6. To establish a library without delay.
7. That one hour of conversation class be held once a week.
8. That an another teacher be engaged immediately to replace
Tsang Tung Ching.
9. That the Health Protection Association be requested to take
responsiblity to hold physical examination on the students.
10. That every convenience be given to the boarding student (For
instance, there is no place for them to wash their faces, rice
bowls and chop-sticks) and that a letter box be fitted enabling
students to offer their opinions to the school authorities.
11. That a "Food Committee" be established.
12. That Mr. Hsia be requested to make a reply to the above
demands and to convene all the students to hold an informal
meeting.
pages.zh:
要求

1. 解雇Tsang Tung Yue（音译）。
2. 公布学校和宿舍规章。
3. 成立“班级联合会”，以促进师生合作。
4. 教师不得干涉任何举行的会议，也不得提出任何建议。
5. 不得随意执行对学生的开除或训诫。
6. 立即建立图书馆。
7. 每周举行一次一小时的话谈课。
8. 立即聘请另一位教师接替Tsang Tung Ching（音译）。
9. 请卫生保护协会负责对学生进行体检。
10. 为寄宿生提供一切便利（例如，目前无处洗脸，无地方放置饭碗和筷子），并安装意见箱，以便学生向校方提出意见。
11. 成立“膳食委员会”。
12. 请夏先生对上述要求作出答复，并召集全体学生举行非正式会议。

Subject. Kiangsu Provincial Middle School of Nantung - present situation
Made by... S.D.I. Chose Liang ...Forwarded by... J.L. Crawford

The Kiangsu Provincial Middle School of Nantung
(江蘇省立南通中學), which was located in Nantung,
northern Kiangsu, and suspended operations following
the occupation of that district by the Japanese
Army in the spring of 1938, resumed classes in
Shanghai at 256 Peking Road about a year ago.
Feng Yoeh Chun (馮樾君) is the Principal of the
School and Yui Teh Zung (于德純), the Dean. It
had some 200 students and is now closed for the
winter vacation.

On November 26, 1939, Feng Yoeh Chun received
by messenger an instructional order dated November 25,
1939 instructing him to hand over the affairs of
the school to Hsia Shih Chong (夏士昌), the new
acting principal of the school. The order
was signed by Mah Yuan Meng (馬元放), former
Commissioner of the Department of Education of the
Kiangsu Provincial Government. Feng Yoeh Chun
disregarded the above mentioned order on the grounds
that he had observed in the newspapers that Mah Yuen
Feng had been deprived of his position as Commissioner
of Education some time ago. Consequently he
refused to hand over the affairs of the school to
the new appointee until he had received special
notification from the proper authorities in the
Kiangsu Provincial Government.

In consequence of this refusal, Hsia Shih Chong,

冯樾君（Feng Yoeh Chun）为该校校长，于德纯（Yui Teh Zung）为教务主任。该校约有学生200名，目前因寒假停课。

NANTUNG MIDDLE SCHOOL STILL OPEN IN SHANGHAI

One year has elapsed since the Nantung
Middle School reopened its classes in Shanghai with the
approval of the Educational Department of the Kiangsu
Provincial Government.
There is no truth in the rumour that the
school in question has been instructed by the Educational
Department of the Kiangsu Provincial Government to move
back to Tungchow.

南通中学仍在上海开课

江苏省立南通中学在江苏省教育厅批准下在上海复课已有一年。

December 26, 1939. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News:

NANTUNG MIDDLE SCHOOL TO BE REORGANIZED

For certain reasons Feng Yueh (馮越), the
Principal of the Nantung Middle School (南通中學) established
by the Kiangsu Provincial Government, has been dismissed by
the Kiangsu Provincial Department of Education, and Hsia
Shih-chong (夏世昌), one of the teachers of the school, has
been appointed to act as Principal.
It is learned that in order to effect a
readjustment of the school affairs, the new Principal has
used Room 11, second floor, House No.53 Foochow Road to
commence registration of students. December 24 being
Sunday, about 200 students called at that address and applied
for registration.
It is also learned that a new site will be
sought for the school to start classes in the near future.
According to registered students, Feng Yueh will wind up
the affairs of the school next week.

5.12.29(PM) NANTUNG MIDDLE SCHOOL PRINCIPAL DEFIES NOTICE OF DISMISSAL

Fung Yoch-chuin (馮桂成君), principal of
the Nantung Middle School (南通中学), publishes the
following notice in the advertisement columns of the "Sin
Wan Pao" and "Shun Pao" to-day :-
    "To the heads of families of the students of
the Nantung Middle School:- On the morning of November 26,
I received Order No.24 issued in Shanghai on November 25 by
Director Ma (馬) of the Education Department of the Kiangsu
Provincial Government, which did not bear the seal of the
document examiner and which reads as follows :-
    'For inefficiency in administration,
the Acting Principal of the school is hereby relieved of
his post and Au Shih-chong (奧士昌) is appointed to
look after the affairs of the school. The Acting
Principal is to hand over his affairs immediately and to
submit a report to this Department for record.'

submitting reports to the Education Department of the Kiangsu

to the school affairs as usual. I publish this notice for
the information of the heads of families of the students to
avoid misleading reports."

南通中学校长冯桂成君（Fung Yoch-chuin，音译，应为冯樾君之误或别名）今日在《新闻报》和《申报》广告栏发布如下通告：

    11月26日上午，我收到江苏省政府教育厅马厅长（Director Ma）于11月25日在上海发布的第24号命令，该命令未加盖文书审核章，内容如下：
    ‘因管理不力，兹免除该校代理校长职务，任命Au Shih-chong（奥士昌，音译，应为夏士昌之误）负责校务。代理校长须立即移交事务，并向本部提交报告备案。’
    “收到此令后，我除向江苏省政府教育厅提交报告请示外，照常处理校务。特此发布通告，告知学生家长，以免误传。”

Central China Daily News :- § - 12. 39 (fm)
BACKGROUND OF DISPUTES BETWEEN STUDENTS AND A LOCAL
MIDDLE SCHOOL

Disputes over political matters have broken
out between the students and the authorities of a certain
local middle school. As this will affect the studies of
the students, the guardians of the students are dissatisfied
with the school management. Up to the present, the school
authorities have done nothing to neutralize the situation.
Last week many teachers and students who favoured peace
were expelled.
Fearing that the situation might become worse,
the school authorities sent a telegram to the Principal
of the school who holds the post of President of the
Educational Department in a certain organization. In reply
the Principal stated that the school should be dissolved.
Recently, the school authorities compelled
the students to enrol in a youth corps and all those who
disregarded the instructions were dismissed for violation
of school regulations.
It is learned that certificates will be issued
to graduates earlier this year. It is alleged that the
maladministration of the school is due to oppression at
the hands of the Chungking Government and Kuomintang. It
is a pity that the school authorities are willing to
sacrifice everything in order to undertake reactionary
activities for Chungking.
pages.zh:
《华中日报》：- § - 1939年12月（上午）

某地一所中学学生与校方之间纠纷的背景

学生与某地一所中学的当局之间爆发了政治问题的纠纷。由于这将影响学生的学业，学生家长对学校管理层表示不满。截至目前，校方未采取任何措施缓和局势。上周，许多主张和平的教师和学生被开除。
校方担心局势可能恶化，遂向该校校长发去电报，该校长在某机构担任教育部门负责人一职。校长回复称，学校应予解散。
最近，校方强迫学生加入青年团，所有无视指令者均因违反校规而被开除。
据悉，今年的毕业证书将提前发放。据称，学校管理不善是由于重庆政府和国民党的压迫所致。遗憾的是，校方为了替重庆进行反动活动，竟愿意牺牲一切。

pages.en:
Sze Tei Wan Pao dated December 8 :- 9.12.3. A/D

TROUBLE IN CERTAIN LOCAL MIDDLE SCHOOL

Of late, trouble has been repeatedly occurring
in a certain middle school in this locality. As this
will affect the studies of the students, all the families
of the students have been very much dissatisfied with the
management o' the school. However, up till the present
moment, the authorities of the school have been unable to
quell the disturbances. Last week clashes occurred during
the course of ejecting some of the opposing teachers and the
peace-loving students. Fearing that this would lead to
serious consequences, the acting authorities o the school
recently sent a telegraphic message for instructions to the
Principal of the school who is at present Commissioner of
Education Bureau of Kansu Province. Unexpectedly after
receiving a reply from the Principal, the attitude of the
authorities of the school became very arrogant and all
students were compelled to join the "Youths' Corps" on pair
of dismissal. All the peace-loving students are much
dissatisfied. The graduation ceremony will be held earlii
earlier this year in order to avoid untoward incidents.
It is learned th:t the reason why the school is doing so
is because the school authorities have received instruction
from the Chungking Government.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》12月8日刊：- 1939年12月9日。A/D

某地一所中学的骚乱

近来，本地某中学屡次发生骚乱。由于这将影响学生的学业，所有学生家长对学校的管理非常不满。然而，直到目前，校方仍无法平息骚乱。上周，在驱逐一些持反对意见的教师和爱好和平的学生过程中发生了冲突。校方担心这会导致严重后果，近期由代理校方人员向现任甘肃省教育局局长的该校校长发电请示。出乎意料的是，在收到校长的回复后，校方的态度变得非常傲慢，并强迫所有学生加入“青年团”，否则予以开除。所有爱好和平的学生对此极为不满。为了避免发生意外事件，毕业典礼将于今年提前举行。
据悉，学校之所以如此行事，是因为校方收到了重庆政府的指示。

先生们，

近期，数名被本校开除的学生频繁闯入我校大楼并制造骚乱。今天他们再次出现，撕毁了我们的课程表。鉴于担心他们可能制造事端，扰乱治安秩序，恳请贵处惠予迅速派遣一名警员来本机构维持秩序，为期十天。我们愿为其提供住宿，并按贵处要求给予津贴。

（盖章）：南通中学。

S.K. Ho:

As a result of interrogation, it was learned
that at about 8 a.m. December 20, 1939, Tsea Hong
and Zung Tse Tae who visited the office of the
Dean Yue Tuh Zung, are alleged to have endeavoured
to force the Dean to leave the school on the
grounds that the Acting Principal, Feng Yoch Chun
and the Dean had disregarded the order of the
Education Department of the Kiangsu Provincial
Government to turn over the affairs of the school
to a new appointee and that they had turned traitors.
According to Feng Yoch Chun, the Acting Princi-
pal, an instructional order dated November 25, 1939,
instructing him to turn over the affairs of the
school to Hsia Sze Chong (夏士宗), the new acting
principal of the school, was sent to him by messenger
on November 26, 1939. The order was signed by
Mah Yuen Feng (馬元豐), the former Commissioner
of Education in the Kiangsu Provincial Government.
Feng Yoch Chun states that he observed in the news-
papers that Mah Yuen Feng had been deprived of his
position as Commissioner of Education some three
months ago, consequently he refused to hand over the
affairs of the school until he has had special
notification from the proper authorities in the
Kiangsu Provincial Government.

据代理校长冯樾君称，一份日期为1939年11月25日的教学指令，指示他将学校事务移交给新任代理校长夏士宗（Hsia Sze Chong，音译），该指令于1939年11月26日由信使送达给他。该命令由前江苏省政府教育厅厅长马元丰（Mah Yuen Feng，音译）签署。
冯樾君称，他在报纸上看到马元丰大约在三个月前已被免去教育厅厅长职务，因此他拒绝移交学校事务，直到收到江苏省政府有关当局的特别通知为止。

1939年12月初，教务长收到一封恐吓信，警告他所谓的叛国行为可能带来的后果。虽然他未向警方报告收到此信，但他强烈怀疑该信出自此次煽动活动的重要元素——孟星平（Mun Sing Ping，音译）所在的源头。然而，他不能确定情况确实如此。所涉恐吓信的译文附后。

December 6, 1939.
Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News . -

THE NANTUNG MIDDLE SCHOOL

It is learned that Au Shih-chong (夏世昌),
the newly appointed principal of the Nantung Middle School
(南通中学), has not been able to take over the school.
Furthermore, Feng Yoeh-chuin (馮樾君), the former acting
principal of the school, has issued a circular notice
addressed to the heads of the families of the students
informing them that although he has received an order of
dismissal, he would nevertheless continue to look after the
affairs of the school. (Translator's note: a translation
of the circular notice was made and included in yesterday
afternoon's translation).

It is reported that the Education Department
of the Kiangsu Provincial Government will adopt effective
means to deal with Feng Yoeh-chuin for disobedience of
orders and, if necessary, it will announce the closure of
the school.

It is generally believed that this school
will probably be ordered to close.
pages.zh:
1939年12月6日。
晨间译文

《中美日报》.-

南通中学

据悉，南通中学新任校长夏世昌未能接管学校。此外，该校前代理校长馮樾君发布了一份通告，致学生家长，告知他们虽然他已收到免职令，但他仍将继续处理学校事务。（译者注：该通告的译文已制作并包含在昨天下午的译文中）。

据报道，江苏省政府教育厅将采取有效措施处理馮樾君违抗命令的行为，如有必要，将宣布关闭该校。

普遍相信，该校可能会被勒令关闭。

DEC 5 1939

NANTUNG MIDDLE SCHOOL PRINCIPAL DEFIES NOTICE OF DISMISSAL

Feng Yoch-chuin (馮桂成君), principal of
the Nantung Middle School (南通中學), publishes the
following notice in the advertisement columns of the "Sin
Wan Pao" and "Shun Pao" to-day :-
"To the heads of families of the students of
the Nantung Middle School:- On the morning of November 6,
I received Order No.24 issued in Shanghai on November 25 by
Director Ma (馬) of the Education Department of the Kiangsu
Provincial Government, which did not bear the seal of the
document examiner and which reads as follows :-
'For inefficiency in administration,
the Acting Principal of the school is hereby relieved of
his post and Au Shih-chong (夏世昌) is appointed to
look after the affairs of the school. The Acting
Principal is to hand over his affairs immediately and to
submit a report to this Department for record.'
"Upon receipt of this order, I, besides
submitting reports to the Education Department of the Kiangsu
Provincial Government asking for instructions, am attending
to the school affairs as usual. I publish this notice for
the information of the heads of families of the students to
avoid misleading reports."

南通中学校长无视免职通知

南通中学校长馮桂成君今日在《新闻报》和《申报》的广告栏刊登如下通知：-
“致南通中学学生家长：- 11月6日上午，我收到江苏省政府教育厅马厅长于11月25日在上海发布的第24号命令，该命令未加盖文书审核印章，内容如下：-
‘因管理不力，兹免去该校代理校长职务，任命夏世昌负责学校事务。代理校长须立即移交事务，并向本部提交报告备案。’
“收到此令后，除向江苏省政府教育厅提交报告请示外，我仍照常处理学校事务。特此发布通知，以供学生家长知悉，避免误导性报道。”

先生，
关于1940年6月19日在刑事分局总部（C.I.）收到的随附匿名信。
1940年6月20日上午，副督察长吴振模（Wu Chen Mo，音译）和下署人采访了康纳路528号暨南大学的秘书长杜佐周先生和校长吴修先生，得知他们均未收到任何威胁，且所述考试即将完成，未发生也预计不会发生任何麻烦，名单上的所有学生均参加了考试。
关于信中提到的四名学生，即：-
1) 金效周，23岁，男，浙江崇德人，居住南京路281号。
2) 戚贵平，20岁，男，江苏永甸人，居住海防路440号。
(b) 23/6

4) Woo Sze Van (吴樹藩), 23, male, native of

Translation of a registered letter received
by Central Station on 18.6.40 from the Chi
Nan University, 528 Connaught Road.

Sir,

I beg to inform you that four students of the
Educational Department of our school named Ching Yao
Tseu (金致周) Zang Kwei Ping (盛貴賓), Woo Tso (吳竺)
and Woo Sze Van (吳樹藩) have joined a terrorist
organization, and have repeatedly carried out terrorist
activities. They were responsible for the assassination
of Sung Sing Woo (宋星五), a teacher of our school.
Ching Yao Tseu and Woo Tso have committed more offences.
It is reported that they will instigate students not to
attend the school examination within this week, and plan
to assassinate Tu Tsoo Tseu (杜佐周), Secretary-General,
and Woo Siu (吳修), Instructor, in an endeavour to
cause detriment to the institute. You are requested to
take strict precaution and immediately arrest them.
(It is suggested that you will arrest them in the school
between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m., Tuesday). You are also requested
to search their domiciles in order to throw light on the
nature of their offences.

Ho Cheu Fee (何去非)
Chi Nan University.

先生，

谨此通知，我校教育部四名学生金致周、盛貴賓、吴竺和吴樹藩加入了一个恐怖组织，并多次实施恐怖活动。他们对我校教师宋星五的暗杀负有责任。金致周和吴竺犯下了更多罪行。据悉，他们将煽动学生在本周内不参加学校考试，并计划暗杀秘书长杜佐周和教员吴修，企图损害学院利益。请采取严格预防措施并立即逮捕他们。（建议您在周二下午2点至4点之间在学校内逮捕他们）。还请您搜查他们的住所，以查明其犯罪性质。

何去非
暨南大学。

Sir,

In the absence of Mr. Ting Sun, President of the
National Chi-nan University, the undersigned in company
with J.I. Chen, interviewed Mr. H.T.C. Tu, Secretary of
the aforementioned institution on the 18-11-39, at 11.15
a.m., regarding questionnaire of D.C. "B" Division.

It was ascertained that no school records had been
removed and neither had any visit been made by unauthor-
ized persons.

Two C.P.C.s have been detailed to patrol Connaught
Road, between Ferry and Hart Roads in the vicinity of
the University, between the hours of 7-00 a.m. and 11-00
p.m. whilst Search Parties have also been instructed to
pay particular attention to this case.

Mr. H.T.C. Tu was informed that in the event of any
untoward incident to immediately inform Gordon Road
Station.

ADMINISTRATION BUILDING
Shanghai, November 17, 1939.
T. Robertson, Esq.,
Deputy Commissioner of Police.
Dear Mr. Robertson,
There has been further information to the
effect that the Pro-Wang terrorists plan to raid the National
Chi-Nan University at 520 Connaught Road and upstairs of 528
Connaught Road. When about a dozen terrorists raided the Chi
Tse College some months ago, they arrived in a truck and finished
the work in a few minutes. It is therefore necessary to guard
the Chi-Nan University at Connaught Road by one or two armed
policeman for, say, two weeks beginning from today. The time
when this extra protection is necessary will be from 7.30 a.m.
to 5 p.m. daily when the faculty and students of the University
are working.
Will you kindly arrange for the necessary
extra protection. Many thanks.
Yours sincerely,
T. K. Ho

Dear Sir:

We have recently learned from two sources
that some terrorists might do some trouble to our
University in the near future. We hope this inform-

the safety of our institution, as well as for the
peace and order of the community, we cordially re-

measures in regard to this matter.

The Chinese-American Weekly, Volume 1, Issue 19, dated
February 3, published the following report :-

SCHOOL PRINCIPAL THREATENED WITH DEATH : PARENTS OF
PUPILS WARNED TO WITHDRAW CHILDREN

A letter containing warnings couched in
strong terms was received by Tsai Chien-ngoo (崔堅吾),
President of the Tao Chung Middle and Primary School
for Girls (道中女子中小學), after he had dispensed with
the services of several teachers of the school, who had
gone over to the rebels. However, due to the undaunted
spirit of the recipient in carrying out reforms at his
school; the senders of this threatening letter were unable
to obtain their objective. Consequently, they fabricated
rumours to the detriment of the school and of its
principal. They even made use of the name of a certain
body and addressed letters to the families of the students
of the school, containing fabrications in the hope of
preventing the students from attending classes. They
again failed to attain their desired object, however,
because their letters have so far been completely ignored
by the families of the students, who are continuing to
send their daughters and sons to the school. This simply
proves that these traitorous elements have failed in
their efforts.

The following is the text of the letter sent
to the families of the students by these traitorous
elements:-

"The management of the Tao Chung Middle and
Primary School for Girls on Avenue Road at the intersection
of Tatung Road is entirely corrupt., Rebel, Tsai Chien-ngoo
is in the habit of profiteering under the pretext of
education; he is skillful in exploitation while administering

(印：(G.L.) DATE 7/2/40)

《中美周刊》第一卷第十九期，2月3日出版，刊登了以下报道：

校长受到死亡威胁：学生家长被警告撤回子女

道中女子中小學（Tao Chung Middle and Primary School for Girls）校长崔堅吾（Tsai Chien-ngoo）在解雇了几名投奔叛军的学校教师后，收到了一封措辞严厉的警告信。然而，由于收信人在推行学校改革方面具有大无畏的精神，这封恐吓信的发送者未能达到其目的。因此，他们编造谣言，损害学校及其校长的声誉。他们甚至利用某个团体的名义，向该校学生家庭寄信，信中充满捏造的内容，企图阻止学生上课。然而，他们再次未能达到 desired object（预期目的），因为迄今为止，学生家庭完全无视这些信件，继续送女儿和儿子上学。这 simply proves（仅仅证明）这些叛国分子的努力失败了。

以下是这些叛国分子向学生家庭发送的信件全文：

“位于大通路（Tatung Road）交汇处的爱文义路（Avenue Road）上的道中女子中小学管理处完全腐败。叛徒崔堅吾习惯于以教育为借口牟取暴利；他在以商业方式管理

（印章：(G.L.) 日期 1940年2月7日）

pages.en:

the school in a business-like manner. He is in receipt
of a $4,000 subsidy every term from certain authorities,
in addition to a monthly salary of $600. Reports to
this effect have appeared in the 'Chinese-American Daily
News,' the 'Ta Mei Pao,' the 'China Press' and the 'China
Weekly Review.' Tsai has long been denounced by the
nation. At one time he went into hiding at a certain
place and dared not come out, entrusting his wife's
relatives with the management of the affairs of the
school. Of late he has again become active. Definite
proof of this has already been secured by this Corps,
thus proving that his guilt is unpardonable. Instructions
have been received from our superior organ to sentence
him to death as a warning to others. The sentence may
be carried out at any time.

"It is indeed a matter for profound regret
that you are still in ignorance of the fact that your
children are being defrauded whilst carrying on their
studies in this school. It is sincerely hoped that they
will at once leave the school and join other institutions,
because we do not wish them to be exposed to danger to
their lives in case of a future mishap. Lest you should
have overlooked the importance of this matter, this
warning is sent you for your information.

"The Shanghai Resistance National
Defence Headquarters. 上海抗衛總部
January 25, 1940."

The following are two letters addressed by
the President of the school to the families of the students
to counteract the above letter sent by the traitorous
elements:-

"Of late information has been received from
students to the effect that certain elements have

学校方面手段娴熟。他每学期从某些当局获得4,000美元的补贴，此外还有每月600美元的薪水。有关此类情况的报道曾出现在《中美日报》、《大美报》、《字林西报》和《密勒氏评论报》上。崔早已受到全国谴责。有一段时间他躲藏在某处，不敢出来，将学校事务委托给妻子的亲属管理。最近他又变得活跃起来。本部队已掌握确凿证据，证明其罪行不可饶恕。已接到上级机关指示，判处其死刑以儆效尤。该判决可随时执行。

“令人深感遗憾的是，你们仍然不知道你们的子女在这所学校读书期间正遭受欺诈。真诚希望他们立即离开该校，转入其他机构，因为我们不希望他们在未来发生意外时面临生命危险。以免你们忽视此事的重要性，特发此警告供你们知悉。

“上海抗衛總部。
1940年1月25日。”

以下是该校校长为抵消上述叛国分子发出的信件而向学生家庭发出的两封信：

the students. As you may be anxious to know these facts,
I therefore send you this letter for your information.---
January 28, 1940."

Second Letter:

"I have been devoting my energies towards
the administration of this school for the past seventeen
years and for this a telegram of encouragement was received
from the Ministry of Education of the National Government
on December 29, last year.

"At the beginning of November last, I went
to Ningpo for the purpose of making preparations for the
establishment of a branch school. However, shortly after
my departure from Shanghai, Ho Ching-yung (何慶榮), Koo
Kung-liang (顧公量), Lu Kung-chao (呂公超) and Chen
Vee-fan (陳維藩), teachers of the school, demanded an
increase of pay and when this was refused, they fabricated
rumours and instigated trouble and finally threatened that
unless the letters of appointment for the next term be
issued and no change in the teaching staff be made, they
would go on strike. In addition, a telegram was received
from the first two mentioned teachers demanding full
rights to deal with the affairs of the school during my
absence. This was evidently an attempt aimed at usurping
my rights over the school. As teachers like these persons
to not deserve further engagement, I rejected all their
demands and returned to Shanghai, with the result that
the affairs of the school have returned to normal.

第二封信：

“过去十七年来，我一直致力于该校的管理工作，为此，去年12月29日收到了国民政府教育部的鼓励电报。

“去年11月初，我前往宁波，目的是为建立分校做准备。然而，在我离开上海后不久，该校教师何慶榮（Ho Ching-yung）、顧公量（Koo Kung-liang）、呂公超（Lu Kung-chao）和陳維藩（Chen Vee-fan）要求加薪，在被拒绝后，他们编造谣言，煽动闹事，最后威胁说，除非发出下学期的聘书且不改变教学人员阵容，否则他们将罢工。此外，还收到前两位提到的教师发来的电报，要求在我缺席期间拥有处理学校事务的全部权利。这显然是一次旨在篡夺我对学校权利的企图。由于像这些人这样的教师不值得继续聘用，我拒绝了他们的所有要求并返回上海，结果学校事务已恢复正常。

January 15, 1940. Morning Translation.

Yesterday an advertisement was published jointly in the "Shun Pao" and "Sin Wen Pao" by Ho Ching-yung, Koo Kung-ling, Chao Wei-ching, Chun Vee-fan and Lu Kung-cho, members of the teaching staff of the school, announcing their resignation. With a view to obtaining some knowledge about the cause of this resignation, a reporter of this paper called at the school yesterday and was informed of the following by Tsai Chien-ngoo, President of the school:-

"I have been looking after the affairs of the school since its establishment some seventeen years ago and have been devoting my entire attention towards the improvement of the affairs of the school because educational enterprises are the foundation of the nation. I have never wavered in my determination towards the support of the national policy for the war of resistance and the observance of the instructions of the Chief Executive of the Kuomintang since the commencement of the war of resistance. This is a fact known to all.

"Recently, a telegram of encouragement was received from Mr. Chen Lih-fu (陳立夫), Minister of Education of the National Government, in recognition of the painstaking efforts I have been undertaking in the upkeep of this school.

"Several months ago, when the conditions in Shanghai were going from bad to worse, I went to Ningpo, on the instructions of the Board of Directors of the school, for the purpose of making preparations for the establishment of a branch school. Before departure, I made known to all the teachers and students of the school the object of this mission, and entrusted the chiefs of the various sections of the school with its affairs. Moreover, they were notified by telegrams of the progress of such preparations when I was in Ningpo. Furthermore, telegrams were also received from Ho Ching-yung and Koo Kung-ling. Unexpectedly, in their advertisement, they alleged that I failed to attend school at the beginning of November last year. This allegation was evidently made with some ulterior motive.

"It is to be noted that shortly after my departure from Shanghai, these teachers at once started trouble. At first they demanded an increase of pay. When this was granted, they instigated the students to create trouble and finally demanded the issue of letters of appointments for the next term and stated that no change was to be made in the teaching staff of the school or else they would declare a strike and extend the trouble. Can this act on their part be regarded as one that was taken in consideration of the heavy responsibilities entrusted to them for the education of the students?

"Moreover, when I was in Ningpo, Ho Ching-yung and Koo Kung-ling telegraphed to me demanding plenipotentiary rights over the affairs of the school. This was evidently intended to seize the control of the school. Are teachers like these worthy of further engagement? Consequently their demands were rejected and this is why they made the allegation in their notice that I had refused to consider or accept their views. As schools are places for the education of youth, I therefore resolved in my mind to start a complete reorganization. Consequently I returned to Shanghai at the end of last year and have now completed all necessary adjustments. I shall continue to work for the development of the school."
pages.zh:
1940年1月15日。晨间译件。

昨日，该校教职员何景容、顾公亮、赵蔚青、陈维藩及吕公超在《申报》和《新闻报》上联合刊登广告，宣布辞职。为了解此次辞职的原因，本报记者于昨日前往该校采访，并从该校校长崔坚吾处获悉以下情况：——

“自十七年前建校以来，我一直负责校务，并因教育事业乃国家之基础而全心致力于改善校务。自抗战爆发以来，我在支持抗战国策及遵守国民党总裁指示方面的决心从未动摇。这是众所周知的事实。

“最近，国民政府教育部长陈立夫先生发来嘉奖电，对我为维持本校所付出的艰辛努力表示认可。

“数月前，鉴于上海局势日益恶化，我奉校董会指示前往宁波，筹备设立分校。临行前，我向全校师生说明了此次出行的目的，并将校务委托给学校各部门主管。此外，我在宁波期间，曾通过电报通报筹备进展。同时，我也收到了何景容和顾公亮的电报。不料，他们在广告中指控我去年十一月初未到校视事。这种指控显然别有用心。

“值得注意的是，在我离开上海后不久，这些教师随即开始闹事。起初他们要求加薪。在获得批准后，他们煽动学生制造麻烦，并最终要求下发下学期的聘书，声称不得变更学校师资队伍，否则将宣布罢工并扩大事态。他们的这种行为能否被视为是对他们所承担的教育学生之重任的考量？

“此外，当我在宁波时，何景容和顾公亮曾发电报给我，要求获得处理校务的全权。这显然是意图夺取学校的控制权。像这样的教师还值得继续聘用吗？因此，他们的要求被拒绝，这就是为什么他们在通告中指控我拒绝考虑或接受他们的观点。由于学校是教育青年的场所，因此我决心进行彻底改组。于是，我在去年底返回上海，目前已完成所有必要的调整。我将继续为学校的发展而努力。”

January 15, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News (comment):-
-RESIGNATION NOTICE OF MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHERS

The following notice published jointly by Lu Kung-chao (呂公超), Chao Wei-ching (趙蔚青), Ho-Ching-yung (何景容), Chen Vee-fan (陳維藩) and Koo Kung-liang (顧公亮), teachers of the Tao Chung Middle and Primary School for Girls (道中女子中小學), announcing their resignation, appeared in the "Shun Pao" and "Sin Wen Pao" on January 14 :-

Since our assumption of teaching posts at the Tao Chung Middle and Primary School for Girls, we have always devoted our entire energy towards the education of the students as well as to assisting Mr. Tsai Chien-ngoo (崔堅吾), the President, in the management of the affairs of the school. However, as the school was established by himself independently, President Tsai refused to consider or accept our proposals. As we are employees and in the interests of education, we considered it unnecessary to insist upon the realization of our views. Unexpectedly, at the beginning of November last year, President Tsai failed to attend school, thereby giving rise to serious hardships in the administration of the school. We intended to tender our resignation upon his return at the end of last year, but in consideration of the heavy responsibilities entrusted to us by the families of the students and with a view to avoiding a discontinuation of the studies, we have been forced to postpone our resignation until to-day. Besides writing to the President to this effect, we publish this notice announcing our resignation from date from all posts at the school, for the information of the public as well as of the families of the students.

-中学教师辞职通告-

道中女子中小学教师吕公超、赵蔚青、何景容、陈维藩和顾公亮联合发布的下列辞职通告，于1月14日刊登在《申报》和《新闻报》上：——

自从我们在道中女子中小学担任教职以来，我们一直全力以赴从事学生教育工作，并协助校长崔坚吾先生管理校务。然而，由于该校系其个人独立创办，崔校长拒绝考虑或接受我们的提议。作为雇员，且出于教育利益的考虑，我们认为没有必要坚持实现我们的观点。不料，去年十一月初，崔校长未到校视事，导致学校管理出现严重困难。我们本打算在他去年底回来时提出辞职，但考虑到学生家长托付给我们的重任，以及为了避免学业中断，我们被迫将辞职推迟至今日。除就此致函校长外，我们特发布此通告，宣布即日起辞去在校的一切职务，以供公众及学生家长知悉。

Made by J. J. l. Liao Shang Chien Forwarded by. J. A. Crawford.

（批：Do B Lingi）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 1939）

As Mr. Tsui (徐江亭), principal of the
Dao Chang Middle School for Girls, No. 566 Avenue,
Road, returned to the school at 2 p.m. December 29,
1939, when a party of police from Jizza Station
maintained order on the premises. Immediately
after his arrival, he made a speech to the students
of the middle school department to the effect that
he had never meddled in politics and that he had
been in Ningpo for the purpose of making arrangements
for the establishment of a branch school there.
He further persuaded the students not to be misled
by trouble makers but to pay attention to their
studies for their own good. Speeches of a similar
nature were also made to students of the primary
school department and the members of the faculty,
the latter being advised to forget everything but
assisting in the development of the school in the
interests of the students and the nation. In his
speeches Mr. Tsui also touched upon the sending of
information on a rumour regarding him to the Chinese
American Daily News and expressed the suspicion that
it must be the work of a certain member of the faculty.
On the same day, copies of a circular issued in
the name of Mr. Tsui, were sent to the families of
all students reporting his return from Ningpo and
assuring them that the administration of school,

Subject Do Chuen Middle School for Girls - return of Tsui Chien Ngoo,
Principal, from Ningpo

Made by D.S.I. Liao Jihua Chien Forwarded by D.I. J.R. Millard

In view of the unsettled state of affairs
in the Do Chuen (道群) Middle School for Girls,
No. 568 Avenue Road, a number of students of which
twice suspended classes, the first time in November,
1939 and the second time in December, 1939, the
principal Tsui Chien Ngoo (徐建吾) has returned
to Shanghai from Ningpo with a view to pacifying
the students. However, he has not attended the
school since his arrival and is keeping his address
strictly secret in order to avoid possible attacks,
it is said, from members of the pro-Wang Ching Wei
party which he joined in June, 1939 but deserted
when he left for Ningpo in November, 1939.

In the afternoon of December 27, 1939,
Lawyer Loh Tsin-Wei (羅振偉), representing Tsui
Chien Ngoo, called at Headquarters and reported
that Tsui intended to attend the school at 2 p.m.
December 29, 1939 to give a lecture to the students
instructing them to pay more attention to their
studies instead of creating unnecessary disturbances
at the instigation of some of the teachers who
have been engaged in a struggle for supremacy in
the institute during his absence. According to
the lawyer, the following teachers are playing an
important role in the present disputes in the school:-

Date. December 21, 1939.
Subject. Mc O ... School for Girls - Students demand
refund of meal expenses.
Made by. D.S.I. Forwarded by. D.C. (Special Branch).

At 11 a.m. December 18, we were informed that boarding
students at the Mc O ... Middle School for Girls,
No. 563 Avenue Road, supported students to press a
demand for a refund of $10.00 of their meal expenses.
These students paid $40.00 a term for meal expenses
during the previous year but in view of the high cost
of food, the sum was increased to $50.00 this term
by order of the school authorities. On the grounds
that the expenses for the meals which are catered for
by the school, do not warrant such an increase, the
students are demanding the restoration of the original
sum and the refund of the $10.00 increase which they
have already paid to the school.

It is reported that the faculty members of the
school divided themselves into factions after the
departure of the Principal, Tsui Chien Kyo (崔堅吾),
for the interior in October, 1939, and are now engaged
in rivalry for power in the administration of the
school. It is said that the teachers who are attached
to one of the factions are behind the present dispute.
By instigating the students to put forth the demand
these teachers hope that they will eventually obtain
sympathy and support from the former.

This school has a total of some 1,400 students
and is in receipt of a grant-in-aid from the Council.

Liao Chung Chien
D.S.I.
D.C. (Special Branch).

制作人：副督察长。转发人：警司（特别支部）。

12月18日上午11时，我们获悉，爱文义路563号麦克奥...女子中学的寄宿学生支持其他学生提出退还10.00元膳食费的要求。这些学生在上一学年每学期支付40.00元膳食费，但鉴于食品价格高涨，校方下令本学期将该费用增加至50.00元。学生们以学校提供的膳食不值如此增幅为由，要求恢复原金额，并退还他们已向学校支付的10.00元增额。

据报，自1939年10月校长崔坚吾（Tsui Chien Kyo）前往内地后，该校教职员工分裂成派系，目前正忙于争夺学校管理权。据说，依附于其中一派系的教师是此次纠纷的背后推手。通过煽动学生提出要求，这些教师希望最终能获得前者的同情和支持。

该校共有学生约1,400名，并接受工部局的津贴补助。

廖仲坚（Liao Chung Chien）

Subject: Tao Chung Middle School for Girls - students suspend studies against expulsion of one of their school-mates.
Made by: D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by: C. Crawford

At ... November 18, 1930, some 30 students of the 2nd class of the Tao Chung Middle School for Girls, 564-570 Avenue Road, suspended studies as a protest against the expulsion of one of their classmates named Lao San Lou (□□□). They, however, resumed class at 10 a.m. the same day after the school authorities promised to permit Lat San Leu to continue her studies in the school on condition that she will refrain in future from inciting her schoolmates to interfere with the administration of the institute.

It is reported that the students in general are dissatisfied with the school authorities for restricting their activities in the school. The school authorities recently forbade the students from introducing anything touching on politics in the wall papers which the latter publish either weekly or monthly and to confine themselves to their studies in view of the prevailing unsettled conditions in Shanghai. The act on the part of the school authorities, however, is regarded by the students as oppressive and they are, therefore, at present agitating for the cancellation of the order.
This school is in receipt of a grant-in-aid from the Council.

Liao Chung Chien
D.S.I.

Date November 7, 1939.
Subject. Anonymous letter alleging principal and students of the Dao Chung
Middle School for Girls of conducting political activities.
Made by D.S.I. Ling Chun Chien Forwarded by

The attached letter purporting to have been signed
by one Chu Chen Nan (朱成南), was received at Police
Headquarters on November 4, 1939. The writer alleges
that (1) a play having a political background is to be
staged in the afternoon of November 4 in the Dao Chung
Middle School for Girls, No.568 Avenue Road, (2) the
principal of the school is taking part in political
activities and has failed to attend school and (3)
radical songs are sung by the students and bulletins
are exhibited on the premises of the institute.

Immediate enquiries ascertained that students of
the 2nd class of the Junior Department of the school,
numbering altogether 92, had arranged to hold a gala
meeting in the afternoon of November 4 for amusement
purposes. The programme to be staged consisted of
the singing of songs mostly taken from foreign films
and Feiping style dramas, containing nothing of an
objectionable nature. However, Ho Ching Yung (何慶榮),
Dean of the school, was communicated at 12.10 p.m.
November 4, 1939 and warned that no meeting would be
allowed unless permission for same was obtained in advance
from the Municipal Police. As a consequence the meeting
was cancelled.

Regarding the allegation that the principal of the
Dao Chung Middle School for Girls is taking part in
political activities and has failed to attend school,

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：Sir, my instructions. E.Y.）

经立即查询查明，该校初中部二年级共92名学生安排于11月4日下午举行联欢会以资娱乐。拟演出的节目包括演唱大多取自外国电影和滑稽剧（Feiping style）的歌曲，不含任何令人反感的性质。然而，1939年11月4日中午12时10分联系了该校教务长何庆荣（Ho Ching Yung），并警告称，除非事先获得警务处许可，否则不允许举行集会。因此，该集会被取消。

Chinese-American Daily News :- 3.11.39(A-1)

DEPARTURE OF EDUCATIONALISTS FROM SHANGHAI

Following the conversion of Shanghai into a
base of lawless activities, local educationalists of
various grades have been encountering coercion and
persuasion from all directions, while a number of these
educationalists have been brutally murdered for having
ignored these approaches. Nevertheless, these outrages
have failed to undermine the loyalty of local educationalists.
Certain educationalists, knowing that they have been marked
down by a certain party, have left Shanghai to avoid
trouble, and by the end of October about 30 had left.
These men are on their way to Szechuen, Yunnan and other
provinces to participate in the war of resistance. On
November 1 another batch of educationalists left Shanghai
for the same reasons.
It is said that Tsui Chien-wu ( 崔 堅 吾 ),
principal of the Dao Chung Middle School for Girls
( 道 中 女 子 中 学 ) is among the second batch. Tsui enjoys
a high repute in local educational circles. A rumour,
which was current at one time that Tsui had betrayed his
honour, was strongly refuted by him. In the face of the
strong pressure that was being brought to bear upon him
by evil influences, Tsui decided to leave. Prior to
his departure, he told his friends that he would establish
schools in the interior and continue in educational work.
All Chinese people express their respect to
these departing educationalists.
pages.zh:
《中美日报》：1939年11月3日 (A-1)

教育家离沪

随着上海沦为无法无天活动的基地，当地各级教育家一直遭受来自各方的胁迫与劝诱，而部分教育家因无视这些手段而惨遭杀害。然而，这些暴行并未能动摇当地教育家的忠诚。某些教育家自知已被某一方盯上，为避祸起见已离开上海，至十月底约有三十人离去。这些人正前往四川、云南等省参加抗战。十一月一日，又有一批教育家出于同样原因离开上海。

据悉，道中女子中学校长崔坚吾属于第二批离沪者。崔氏在当地教育界享有盛誉。此前曾有关于崔氏失节的谣言流传，但遭到其强烈驳斥。面对恶势力施加的巨大压力，崔氏决定离开。临行前，他告诉友人，将在内地创办学校，继续从事教育工作。全体中国人民对这些离去的教育家表示敬意。

COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE.

October 31, 1939.

The Police Department,

Gentlemen,

I beg to inform you that the principal of the Tao
Chung Girl School, corner of Avenue and Tatung Roads,
where my children are now studying, has been absent from
the school as he is taking part in political activities,
while the faculty and the students are often involved in
disputes owing to their party difference with the result
that the school is in a disorderly condition, according
to the verbal report of my children.

With a view to verifying it I have proceeded to the
above-mentioned school and, during the tour of inspection,
found numerous of bulletins on the wall and heard many
radical songs in the classrooms.

It is truly due to the allegations against the prin-
cipal Chuen Kien-Wu made in the China Weekly Review, in
the Ta Ying Pao and in the China-American Daily News that
he has not stayed in the school for more than one month.

A "Dialogue" play having political background, according
to the staff of the school, is to be staged on the Saturday
afternoon of October 4, 1939 when both parties will probably
come to blows.

1月4日下午4时30分，约40名罗氏学院学生自治会骨干成员在南京路490号一楼的学院内举行会议，由该会主席杨宝赓主持。一名叫陈松荣的人提议就公众对中日敌对行动的态度进行调查。该提议具有亲汪精卫和平运动的性质。当主席提出反对意见时，引发了争执。

Shun Pao publishes in its advertisement columns the following
urgent notice inserted by the Chairmen of the Boards of
Directors and the Principals of the Shanghai Middle School,
the Shanghai Primary School, the Shanghai Normal School and
the Shanghai Kindergarten :-

Education is a public enterprise, while schools
are public property. It is on this principle that the
Government has always been paying particular attention to
and encouraging the promotion of education as well as the
establishment of schools in the country. Consequently, there
is not the least doubt that the four schools above mentioned
belong to this category and are, therefore, the property of
the public.

Considering that these four educational
institutions are public property and in our consideration of
the studies of several thousand students, we have taken up
concurrently the posts of Principals of these schools
following the retirement of the ex-Principal Chen Chi-zing,
with the object of maintaining these institutions. We
absolutely deny that schools are private property. Lest
the public should still be ignorant of this, this notice
is published hereby for their information.

Yu Ya-ching,

1.

Trouble at Shanghai Middle School.
At 10.50a.m. on 17-5-40 C.P.C. 3098 reported to
this station by telephone that students were causing
a disturbance in the Shanghai Middle School, 460
Chengtu Road.
A party of Police under Inspector Blenkinsop,
officer i/c, attended, and on arrival found that a
number of desks, forms, and windows had been smashed
by the students.
From enquiries made by C.D.S. 71 and the under-
signed, the following was ascertained:-
On 10-5-40 an article appeared in the Chinese-
American Daily News, a Chinese language newspaper, to
the effect that the Shanghai Middle School was owned
by one Zung Chi Zung (陈济成), who is President of
the Overseas Students Board of the Nanking Government.
On 12-5-40 the principal Ling Kaung Heu (林康侯),
published a denial in the above newspaper
and announced that Zung Chi Zung had severed all
connection with the school sometime ago. On the
morning of 17-5-40, however, a further article appeared
in the Chinese-American Daily News to the effect the
above denial was useless, as there was definite proof
that Zung Chi Zung was still connected with the school.
On arriving at the school on the morning of

上海中学骚乱。
1940年5月17日上午10时50分，中央巡逻车3098号通过电话向本站报告，称学生在成都北路460号的上海中学制造骚乱。
由督察 Blenkinsop 率领的一队警察到场，到达后发现许多课桌、长凳和窗户被学生砸坏。
经刑事侦缉小队71号和本人询问，查明情况如下：
1940年5月10日，中文报纸《中美日报》刊登一篇文章，称上海中学归南京政府海外学生委员会主席陈济成所有。
1940年5月12日，校长林康侯在上述报纸上发表否认声明，并宣布陈济成已在不久前与学校断绝一切联系。然而，1940年5月17日上午，《中美日报》又刊登一篇文章，称上述否认无效，因为有确凿证据证明陈济成仍与学校有关联。
当天上午到达学校时，

because of this article, and about 10.45a.m. they
began to damage the school property. After the

with the principal. The remainder of the students
left the premises, and the school was closed for
the day. A notice will be posted on 18-5-40 announc-
ing the result of the discussions.

At the request of the principal, all police were
withdrawn from the school at 11.45a.m. on 17-5-40.

At about 11 a.m., May 17, students of the
Middle School Department of the Shanghai Private
Middle School, 460 Chengtu Road, ceased to attend
class and a number of them resorted to acts of
violence by smashing windows and several desks in
their class rooms.

Enquiries reveal that the agitation
started among the students of the senior 3rd class
and arose out of a news article which appears in
the Chinese American Daily News of May 17, alleging
that the school is the property of Mr. CHEN CHI ZUNG
(陈济成), now Chairman of the Overseas Chinese
Affairs Committee of the Wang Ching Wei sponsored
New Central Government. An article first appeared
in the May 10th Issue of the paper in question, but
an announcement to refute the allegation was made
by the school authorities on May 12. Another article
containing a similar allegation, however, again made
its appearance in to-day's issue of the Chinese
American Daily News, and the students demand a
definite explanation from the school authorities
concerning its standing. They are of the opinion
that the allegation is detrimental to the students
as a whole, and they would sever their connections
with the institute unless the authorities made
known to the public the attitude of the school.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C.B REGISTRY Date May 17, 1940.）
（印：SHANGHAI 18 MAY 1940 COMMIS. IUNER'S OFFICE）

5月17日上午11时许，成都路460号上海私立中学中学部的学生停止上课，其中部分学生采取暴力行为，砸碎了教室内的窗户和几张课桌。

经查询得知，此次骚动始于高三年级学生，起因是5月17日《中美日报》刊登的一篇新闻文章，该文章声称该校是汪精卫赞助的新中央政府侨务委员会主席陈济成（CHEN CHI ZUNG）先生的私产。有关报纸首先在5月10日的一期中刊登了类似文章，但校方于5月12日发布公告予以驳斥。然而，《中美日报》今日刊出的文章中再次出现了类似的指控，学生们要求校方就其立场作出明确解释。他们认为该指控损害了全体学生的利益，除非校方向公众阐明学校的态度，否则他们将切断与该机构的关系。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 C.B 登记处 日期 1940年5月17日。）

Following this agitation, the school
authorities issued a notice, stating that the
middle school and elementary normal school
departments would be closed for the time being,
but expect to resume classes next week. They also
intend to insert an advertisement in the local
newspaper explaining the standing of the institute.
This school consists of four departments,
namely the middle school, elementary normal school,
the primary school and kindergartens, with a total
of 1,600 students. About 600 students of the
middle school and 200 of the elementary normal
school departments are affected by the present
unrest, while the remainder are attending class
as usual.

It will be remembered that the Shanghai
Private Middle School came into existence in 1924
with Mr. CHEN CHI ZUNG as its founder. CHEN was
a pro-Chungking Government member until the
beginning of June, 1939, when he established
connections with the pro-Wang Ching Wei elements.
In consequence of his change in attitude, agitation
was rife among the students during the summer of
1939 and CHEN resigned in September, 1939, handing
over the affairs of the school to the Board of
Directors which consist of Messrs. YU YA CHING
(虞洽卿), YUAN LIU TENG (袁履登), WEN LAI TING

需指出的是，上海私立中学成立于1924年，创办人为陈济成（CHEN CHI ZUNG）先生。陈一直是支持重庆政府的成员，直到1939年6月初，他开始与亲汪精卫分子建立联系。由于其态度转变，1939年夏季学生中骚动频发，陈于1939年9月辞职，将校务移交给董事会，董事会成员包括虞洽卿（YU YA CHING）、袁履登（YUAN LIU TENG）、闻兰亭（WEN LAI TING）

May 17, 1940.
Afternoon Translation

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following article:-

THE SHANGHAI MIDDLE SCHOOL

On May 10 the editor of this paper published a note in reply to a reader enquiring about the Shanghai Middle School. The following passage appeared in the reply: "The Shanghai Middle School is the private property of Chen Che-chen (陳濟成), Chairman of the puppet Chinese Overseas Affairs Committee of Wang Ching-wei's puppet regime. Do you think you can study in that school?"

The next day we received a letter from the Shanghai Middle School written on paper inscribed as follows: "General Office of the Shanghai Middle School, the Shanghai Normal School, the Shanghai Primary School and the Shanghai Kindergarten."

Stating that they were greatly astonished by our reply, the writers went on:- "Chen Che-chen left this school long ago. Necessary procedure has been adopted by the Board of Directors of the school to apply to the Ministry of Education in Chungking for a change of the headmaster of the school. Sanction was granted. What your letter alleged not only affects the reputation of this school and the work of our students but is against the order of the Government."

This newspaper was finally requested to publish a correction.

The allegations contained in the letter are absolutely untrue. Nobody can deny that the four schools, namely, the Shanghai Middle School, the Shanghai Normal School, the Shanghai Primary School and the Shanghai Kindergarten, are the private property of Chen Che-chen. Prior to the time that Chen joined the other party, any one of these four schools could use the letter-heads inscribed "General Office of the Shanghai Middle School, the Shanghai Normal School, the Shanghai Primary School and the Shanghai Kindergarten." Last summer we exposed the fact of Chen's secession, but Chen tried to deny it. The same kind of letter-head was used when he wrote to this newspaper to give his cunning denial. We still have that letter in hand and an investigation can be easily made.

The administration of a school should be independent. If these four schools are not the property of a private individual, then how could there be a "General Office?" Granted that the four schools are the property of a private individual (but not that of Chen Che-chen), then whose property are they? Does it mean that this "General Office of the Shanghai Middle School, the Shanghai Normal School, the Shanghai Primary School and the Shanghai Kindergarten" has been granted registration by the Ministry of Education of Chungking?

It is obvious that it was when these four schools formerly belonged to Chen Che-chen that the unlawful body called the "General Office of the four schools" was formed. As these four schools are at present still the private property of Chen Che-chen, this illegal body is still functioning.

Should we be required to probe the matter further, let us ask who is Yang Hwa (楊華), secretary of the puppet Chinese Overseas Affairs Committee, and who is Wang Lieh (汪立)? As regards the $7,000 a month and so forth, this is a matter of common knowledge. Does this mean that some substitute is required to play the tricks to which Chen Che-chen resorted last summer?

1940年5月17日。
下午译文

《中美日报》刊登以下文章：-

上海中学

5月10日，本报编辑发表了一篇回复读者关于上海中学询问的便函。回复中出现了以下段落：“上海中学是汪精卫伪政权伪中国侨务委员会主席陈济成（Chen Che-chen）的私产。你认为你能在那所学校读书吗？”

第二天，我们收到一封来自上海中学的信，信纸抬头印有：“上海中学、上海师范学校、上海小学及上海幼稚园总办事处。”

写信人称对我们的回复感到极为震惊，接着写道：“陈济成早已离开本校。学校董事会已采取必要程序，向重庆教育部申请更换校长。获批。贵报来信所述不仅影响本校声誉及我校学生工作，且违背政府法令。”

最后要求本报刊登更正声明。

信中所含指控完全不实。无人能否认，上海中学、上海师范学校、上海小学及上海幼稚园这四所学校是陈济成的私产。在陈加入另一方之前，这四所学校中的任何一所都可以使用印有“上海中学、上海师范学校、上海小学及上海幼稚园总办事处”字样的信头。去年夏天我们揭露了陈分裂的事实，但陈试图否认。他在给本报写信进行狡辩否认时，使用了同样的信头。我们手中仍存有那封信，调查易如反掌。

学校管理应当独立。如果这四所学校不是个人的私产，那么怎么会有“总办事处”呢？假设这四所学校是私人的财产（但不是陈济成的），那是谁的财产呢？这是否意味着这个“上海中学、上海师范学校、上海小学及上海幼稚园总办事处”已获得重庆教育部的注册批准？

显然，当这四所学校以前属于陈济成时，才形成了名为“四校总办事处”的非法团体。由于这四所学校目前仍是陈济成的私产，这个非法团体仍在运作。

若需进一步探究此事，让我们问问谁是伪中国侨务委员会秘书杨华（Yang Hwa），以及谁是汪立（Wang Lieh）？至于每月7,000美元等等，这是众所周知的事。这是否意味着需要某个替身来施展陈济成去年夏天所用的伎俩？

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S.I. Special Branch 614661
REPORT
Date September 12, 1939

Subject Shanghai Middle School - 460 Chengtu Road

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung-chien Forwarded by R W Mac (signature)

Chen Chi-zung (陳濟成), principal of the
Shanghai Middle School, 460 Chengtu Road, resigned
from his position in the school on September 10,
1939, in order to pacify the students who are agitating
against his attitude which favours the peace
movement advocated by Wang Ching Wei.

At noon, September 12, Messrs Yuan Lu-tung,
and Yu Ya Ching, Chinese Councillors of the S.M.C.,
Ling Kong Hou, Secretary of the Bankers' Association
and Vung Lai Ding (聞蘭亭), Chairman of the
Federation of Charitable Organisations, 35 Yunnan Road,
who are four principal members of the Board of
Directors of the Shanghai Middle School, met in the
Bankers' Association, 59 Hongkong Road and decided
that the affairs of the school be handled by the
Board of Directors with Ling Kong Hou as
representative and no new principal be appointed
in place of Chen Chi-zung resigned.

This school had a total of 2,400 students
during the last term. However, as a result of
the dispute over the political status of Chen Chi-zung,
some 700 failed to register with the school for the
current term.

Liao Chung Chien
D.S.I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

上海中学（成都路460号）校长陈济成（Chen Chi-zung）于1939年9月10日辞去校内职务，以平息因他支持汪精卫倡导的和平运动的态度而引发的学生骚动。

9月12日中午，工部局华人董事袁履登先生和虞洽卿先生、银行公会秘书林康侯先生、以及云南路35号慈善团体联合会主席闻兰亭（Vung Lai Ding）先生——此四人为上海中学董事会的主要成员——在香港路59号银行公会会面，决定由董事会处理校务，由林康侯担任代表，且不任命新校长接替辞职的陈济成。

上学期该校共有学生2,400名。然而，由于陈济成政治地位的争议，本学期约有700名学生未到校注册。

August 15. 39.

Chen Chi Zung , Headmaster of the Shanghai Middle
School - allegations contained in an anonymous letter addressed
to the Shanghai Municipal Police

On August 18th 1939, a letter in the form
of an official despatch was received at Police
Headquarters. This letter which bears the seal
of an organization entitled "Shanghai Various Circles
National Salvation Federation", alleges that Chen
Chi-zung, principal of the Shanghai Middle School,
460 Chengtu Road, has allied himself with Wang Ching
Wei's Clique and has been in receipt of subsidy from
them. His duties, according to the letter,
consist of exploiting teachers and students of local
Chinese schools for the benefit of Wang's cause,
conducting pro-Wang and anti-British propaganda,
supplying the "enemy" with information on the military
and political secrets of the National Government as
well as the activities of the authorities of the
Foreign Settlements at Shanghai.

Chen Chi-zung, native of Kading, Kiangsu,
age 45, is a committee member of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council and lives at 3/179 Connaught Road. A
summary of his past activities is appended to this
report.

He is unscrupulous but smart. The record
shows that in the past he was an ardent supporter of
the national salvation movement and participated in
all kinds of movements which would bring him before
the public eye, but undoubtedly his real object has
been to attain prominence in social as well as
political circles so as to pave the way for his own

1939年8月15日。

陈继曾，上海中学校长——致上海公共租界工部局警务处的一封匿名信中所含指控

1939年8月18日，警察总局收到一封以官方公文形式发出的信件。这封信盖有一个名为“上海市各团体救国联合会”的组织的印章，指控成都路460号上海中学校长陈继曾与汪精卫派系勾结，并收受其津贴。据该信称，他的职责包括利用当地华校师生为汪氏事业谋利，进行亲汪反英宣传，向“敌人”提供国民政府的军事和政治机密以及上海外国租界当局的活动情报。

陈继曾，江苏嘉定人，45岁，系上海公共租界工部局华董，居住于康纳脱路179号3室。本报告附录了其过往活动摘要。

他为人精明但无原则。记录显示，他过去曾是救国运动的热烈支持者，并参与各种能使其受到公众关注的运动，但无疑其真实目的是在社会及政治圈中获得显赫地位，从而为其自身

ends. In this respect he has achieved much success.
Through his position as principal of a school
having more than 4,000 students, he succeeded in
attracting the attention of the local Chinese community
in 1930. His ardour in national salvation movements
following the outbreak of the local Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937, gradually turned the attention
into respect and won over the confidence and support
of the Chinese people.
Consequently, at the beginning of June, 1939,
when Wang Ching Wei's clique decided to undermine
General Chiang's influence in Shanghai through edu-
cational circles, Chow Vuh-hai (周佛海), right-
hand man of Wang in the peace movement, approached
Chen with handsome bribes. Chen succumbed and
in the middle of June, 1939 he succeeded in enlisting
the cooperation of six others and formed a committee
known as "Shanghai Educational Committee (上海教育
委員會)" also known as "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Edu-
cational Circles' Branch (中國國民黨教育界支部)".
with Chen himself as the Chairman. Among the
six persons, four are known to be the following persons :-
Feng Ih-sien (一先) Principal of the Min
Kuo (民國) Middle School, 1/289
Weihaiwei Road.
Tsui chien Ngo (崔堅吾), Principal of the Dao
Chung Middle School for Girls (道
中女子中學), 628 Avenue Road.
Zi Tsuh Hsiang (徐則驤), dean of the Ming Kwang

因此，在1939年6月初，当汪精卫派系决定通过教育界破坏蒋介石将军在上海的影响力时，汪在和平运动中的得力助手周佛海以重金贿赂接触陈继曾。陈继曾屈服了，并于1939年6月中旬成功拉拢另外六人合作，组建了一个名为“上海教育委员会”的委员会，亦称“中国国民党教育界支部”，由陈继曾本人担任主席。在这六人中，已知有四人为以下人士：
冯一先，民国中学校长，威海卫路289号1室。
崔坚吾，道中女子中学校长，爱文义路628号。
徐则驤，明光中学教务主任，胶州路

In turn for the appointment, they are said to have
each signed a pledge form supporting Wang Ching Wei's
cause. Chen's salary is $600 per mensem while
the other committee members receive $300 each monthly.
In addition a monthly sum of $5,000 has been granted
to the Committee for use in buying over the allegiance
of local middle and primary schools at the rate of
between $100 and $200 per month for middle schools
and between $50 and $80 for primary schools. It
is reported that up to the present time some 50
schools have joined Chen and thus benefited by this
money; the names of the schools however cannot be
ascertained at present.

Because of fear of reprisals from the Chung-
king Government the Committee have so far refused to
conduct the pro-Wang movement in the open, despite
repeated persuasion from their employers. The
latter insisted upon the former making public their
support of Wang's cause for the following reasons :-
to prevent the committee members from reverting in
future, to convince the public of the extent of Wang's
influence in Shanghai and to induce others to join.

Becoming impatient with the secretive
attitude of these followers, Wang's clique decided
to employ indirect methods to force their hands.

据称，作为任职的交换条件，他们每人都签署了一份支持汪精卫事业的保证书。陈继曾的月薪为600元，其他委员每人每月领取300元。此外，委员会每月还获得5000元的拨款，用于收买当地中小学的效忠，中学每月100至200元，小学每月50至80元。据报道，截至目前，约有50所学校加入了陈继曾的阵营并从中受益；然而，目前尚无法查明这些学校的名称。

由于害怕重庆政府的报复，尽管雇主反复劝说，该委员会至今拒绝公开开展亲汪运动。后者坚持要求前者公开支持汪氏事业，理由如下：防止委员会成员日后反悔，让公众相信汪氏在上海的影响力范围，并诱使其他人加入。

汪精卫派系对这些追随者的秘密态度感到不耐烦，决定采取间接手段迫使他们就范。
